title: Lifetime Launch System
body_html:
The Estes Lifetime Launch System is the first and only launch system designed specifically for educators, youth leaders, and group programs. Built for repeated use, this durable system ensures dependable performance launch after launch, all while keeping students engaged and excited about rocketry. Standing 18 inches tall, the launch pad gives students plenty of room to safely load and service rockets before sending them skyward.

Durability You Can Trust

True to its name, the Lifetime Launch System is backed by a Lifetime Limited Warranty, making it a long-term investment for any classroom or program. Its sturdy construction is designed to endure repeated use, ensuring that it remains a reliable piece of equipment for years to come.

Complete and Versatile Setup

Each system comes with a Pro Series II Launch Controller and 30 feet of cable, giving you the flexibility to position students at a safe distance during launches. The adjustable launch rod holder accommodates both included rods—1/8 inch and 3/16 inch—making it suitable for a variety of rockets, from beginner kits to more advanced designs.

Safety and Learning Combined

The Pro Series II Controller features an audible continuity system that confirms when the starter is properly connected. Students can hear the confirmation before launch, boosting confidence and ensuring safe ignition every time. This feature is especially valuable in group learning environments where clarity and safety are top priorities.

Easy to Build, Easy to Use

Assembly is simple with just pliers or a 7/16 socket and wrench (tools not included). Once built, the Lifetime Launch System provides an intuitive and engaging platform for teaching rocketry, making it the perfect choice for classrooms, summer camps, and STEM-focused programs.

title: Tazz™
body_html:
A classic Estes kit re-imagined.

The specially designed engine mount has two molded tabs. These tabs hold the wing elevators in the flat position during boost for nice straight-up flights. Then at apogee, the ejection charge kicks the engine mount out and “snap”, the two elevators move into the full “up” position and TAZZ Estes rocket spins wildly on the way down!

Larger than the 1960's "Gyroc" kit, this rocket model has balsa wings with alignment tabs that fit into pre-cut slots. This makes aligning the wings much easier during assembly and after the glue is dry. Moreover, you also get a strong wing-to-tube glue joint.

The clever molded plastic retainers make installing and replacing the elevator actuator rubber bands very easy.

You can’t count the number of spins this Tazz Estes rocket will make on the way down. What you can do is counting on it for lots of fun flights!

A classic Estes kit re-imagined, featuring:

  • Specially designed engine mount with two molded tabs that hold the wing elevators in the flat position during boost for nice straight-up flights, and then move them into the full "up" position at apogee for wild spins on the way down
  • Balsa wings with alignment tabs that fit into pre-cut slots, making aligning the wings much easier during assembly and after the glue is dry, and providing a strong wing-to-tube glue joint
  • Clever molded plastic retainers that make installing and replacing the elevator actuator rubber bands very easy
  • Lots of fun flights with countless spins on the way down

title: BT-65 Body Tube
body_html:
The BT-65 Body Tube is built for rocketeers who want to scale up their next Estes project. With a 23.5 inch length and strong spiral wound paper construction, it gives custom builders a dependable airframe for larger rockets, replacement work, and high-impact launch-day designs.

A Larger Tube for More Ambitious Builds

BT-65 sizing gives you more presence on the launch pad and more space to plan the rocket around your goals. Whether you are designing a clean single-body rocket or building something taller with compatible couplers and nose cones, this tube gives your project a strong place to start.

Designed for 29 mm Engine Projects

When used with the proper 29 mm to BT-65 laser cut ring set and related engine mounting components, the BT-65 Body Tube can support rockets built around Estes E16 or F15 model rocket engines. That added power makes it a great option for hobbyists who want a larger rocket with exciting lift, strong performance, and a dramatic climb.

Great for TARC-Style Rocketry

Pair this body tube with compatible BT-65 components to create a rocket that can reach over 4 feet tall, including egg lofting designs inspired by TARC competition requirements. The BT-65 Body Tube is also used in the Green Eggs and Olympus rockets, giving builders a proven Estes part for serious custom projects.

title: Mini Blaster™ Air Rocket Launch Set
body_html:
The Mini Blaster™ Air Rocket Launch Set brings high flying excitement to outdoor play using simple air powered launches. With no engines, batteries, or electronics involved, this set is easy to use and perfect for introducing kids to the thrill of rocketry in a hands on way.

Instant Fun With Simple Air Power

Launching is fast and intuitive. Attach the rocket, step on the pump, and watch it blast into the sky. The straightforward design means less setup time and more time enjoying repeat launches.

Designed for Safe, Active Play

Lightweight rockets and air powered launches make this set ideal for family friendly fun. Kids can stay active outdoors while developing coordination and curiosity through play.

Portable and Built for Repeat Launches

The compact design makes it easy to bring the Mini Blaster to the backyard, park, or open field. Rockets are reusable, allowing for launch after launch without extra supplies.

Important Compatibility Information

The Mini Blaster™ Air Rocket Launch Set is designed exclusively for Mini Blaster air rockets. The Whirlwind™ Air Rocket Replacement, Zolt™ & Volt™ Air Rockets, and the T-Bolt™ Replacement Air Rocket are not compatible with this launch system.

title: BT-80 Body Tube
body_html:
The BT-80 Body Tube gives experienced rocketeers a larger canvas for building rockets with more presence, more payload space, and more design flexibility. Made from sturdy spiral-wound kraft paper, this 23.5 inch tube is a dependable starting point for custom airframes, replacement builds, and rockets designed to stand out on launch day.

Designed for Bigger Rocket Builds

With its large BT-80 size, this body tube is ideal for creating impressive single-stage rockets or extended designs using multiple tubes. Pair it with BT-80 Tube Couplers, PN 3178, when you want additional body length for payload sections, egg-lofting layouts, or a taller custom rocket profile.

Ready for 24 mm and 29 mm Configurations

The BT-80 Body Tube can be configured for Estes 24 mm or 29 mm engines when used with the proper motor mount components. Builders can also pair it with the Laser Cut Ring Set, PN 068254, to create a solid foundation for larger power setups and more ambitious flight plans.

A Strong Choice for Payload and Competition Projects

For hobbyists and TARC teams, the BT-80 Body Tube offers the size and strength needed for egg-lofting rockets, payload bays, and competition-inspired designs. Finish the profile with an NC-80K or NC-80B nose cone, then bring your own design to life with the stability, scale, and performance potential that BT-80 projects are known for.

title: BT-65 Tube Coupler
body_html:
The BT-65 Tube Coupler is built for rocketeers who want to customize, repair, or extend their BT-65 body tube rockets with confidence. Measuring 4 inches long, this coupler slips inside compatible BT-65 body tubes to create a clean, strong connection between sections.

Extend Your Rocket Design

Whether you are increasing body tube length for a custom build or replacing a needed part, this BT-65 coupler gives you the flexibility to build the rocket you have in mind. Its 4 inch length offers a reliable bonding area, helping create a sturdy joint that supports a smooth, streamlined rocket body.

Build Payload Bays and Custom Sections

The BT-65 Tube Coupler can also be used as a shoulder joint when adding a payload bay to your rocket. With an ID of 1.684 inches and an OD of 1.744 inches, it is a practical component for builders who enjoy experimenting with new configurations, added sections, and functional rocket designs.

A Useful Replacement and Builder Part

This coupler is used in the Estes Green Eggs and Olympus rockets, making it a smart part to have on hand for repairs, replacements, or future builds. Add one to your workshop and keep your next BT-65 model rocket project moving from idea to launch pad.

title: NC-80K Nose Cone
body_html:
The NC-80K Nose Cone is built for rocketeers who want to bring a polished, aerodynamic look to their BT-80 model rocket projects. Its sleek shape gives your rocket a more finished profile, whether you are designing a custom build from scratch or replacing a worn part on an existing favorite.

Designed for BT-80 Rocket Builds

This plastic nose cone is made to fit BT-80 size body tubes, making it a reliable choice for larger model rocket designs. It gives builders a dependable starting point for creating rockets with bold proportions, strong visual presence, and exciting launch-day performance.

Lightweight, Durable Construction

Blow molded from high impact styrene plastic, the NC-80K delivers the balance builders want in a model rocket nose cone. It is lightweight enough to help support stable flight while still offering the durability needed for repeated handling, building, and recovery.

Easy Recovery System Attachment

A molded eyelet in the base makes it simple to attach a shock cord and parachute shroud lines. That built-in feature helps streamline your build, so you can spend less time modifying parts and more time getting your rocket ready for the next countdown.

title: HBT BT-1000 3.98 Inch Body Tube
body_html:
The HBT BT-1000 3.98 Inch Body Tube is a thick-walled engine mount tube designed for 24 mm model rocket motors. Whether you are replacing a worn part, restoring a favorite rocket, or laying out a custom design, this tube gives your motor mount a strong and dependable starting point.

Built for 24 mm Rocket Motors

This body tube is sized for 24 mm diameter engines, making it a useful component for hobbyists working with larger low-power rocket designs. Its compact length keeps the build efficient while still giving the engine mount the support it needs.

Strong, Clean, and Easy to Work With

The thick-walled white tube offers the durability builders want when assembling a secure motor mount. With a .95 inch inside diameter and 1.0 inch outside diameter, it is made for a clean fit in compatible Estes rocket builds and custom projects.

A Smart Part for Your Rocket Bench

Small parts make a big difference when you are building with confidence. Keep the HBT BT-1000 3.98 Inch Body Tube on hand so you are ready for your next repair, modification, or 24 mm-powered rocket project.

title: Quik Cure Epoxy (5 Minutes)
body_html:
Quik Cure Epoxy is the ideal solution when you need a strong bond in a short amount of time. This two-part adhesive is formulated to set in just 5 minutes, making it a reliable option for small repairs, model assembly, or last-minute fixes. Within one hour, the epoxy reaches its full strength, creating a bond that lasts.

Fast and Reliable Performance

Time-sensitive projects demand an adhesive that works as quickly as you do. Quik Cure Epoxy mixes easily and cures fast, eliminating long wait times while ensuring your build or repair holds firm. Whether you’re working on hobby projects or quick household fixes, it gets the job done efficiently.

Durable, Lasting Bond

Despite its rapid curing time, Quik Cure Epoxy doesn’t compromise on strength. Once fully cured, the bond resists stress and wear, providing dependable durability. It’s designed for materials and surfaces that need a lasting hold even under demanding conditions.

Perfect for Small-Scale Applications

This epoxy is best suited for small areas or targeted repairs where precision and speed are essential. For larger surfaces or extended working time, consider using Mid-Cure or Slow-Cure epoxy options. Quik Cure ensures you always have the right tool for the right project.

title: Mid Cure Epoxy (15 Minutes)
body_html:
Mid-Cure Epoxy is designed for model rocketry and hobby applications where more time is needed for assembly. With a 15-minute set time, it provides ample working time to position parts correctly, making it the go-to choice for large surface areas and detailed builds. Builders will appreciate the control and confidence this adhesive provides when precision is essential.

Strong and Flexible Bond

Unlike quick-set formulas, Mid-Cure offers greater flexibility once cured, which helps absorb stress and impact from launches and recoveries. This flexibility makes it less brittle, reducing the risk of cracking under pressure. It also cures to a tough, durable finish that stands up to repeated use.

Water Resistant Performance

One of the standout benefits of Mid-Cure Epoxy is its superior water resistance. Whether your rocket encounters damp conditions, morning dew, or light moisture during landing, this adhesive keeps your components securely bonded. It’s built to endure both environmental and flight stresses.

Reliable Curing Process

Mid-Cure begins to set in 15 minutes, giving you time to carefully assemble your rocket components. After 2 hours, the bond reaches its full strength, ensuring your model is ready for high-performance launches. Each 4.5 oz. package provides enough epoxy for multiple projects, making it a dependable staple in any rocketeer’s toolkit.

title: Slow Cure Epoxy (30 Minutes)
body_html:
Slow-Cure Epoxy provides the extra working time needed for detailed assembly and careful alignment. Its 30-minute set time ensures you won’t have to rush, allowing for cleaner and stronger bonds when precision matters most.

Strength That Lasts

After curing for 24 hours, this epoxy achieves its full bonding strength, ensuring a reliable hold that resists stress and impact. Designed for long-term durability, it stands up to repeated launches and recoveries without weakening.

Made for Harsh Conditions

Engineered to be both waterproof and heat resistant, Slow-Cure Epoxy is built to perform under demanding conditions. From hot ejection charges to outdoor moisture, this adhesive maintains its bond through it all.

A Must-Have for Hobbyists

Whether you’re reinforcing a critical joint or assembling an entire rocket, this epoxy is versatile enough for large surfaces and small details alike. With its dependable formula and ample 4.5 oz. supply, Slow-Cure Epoxy is an essential tool in every rocketeer’s workshop.

title: No 1 Light Duty Knife
body_html:

title: C11-3 Engine Bulk Pack
body_html:
The C11-3 Engine Bulk Pack gives you twelve ready-to-fly C-class motors engineered for consistent lifts and eye-catching altitudes. Each motor produces a strong but controllable burst of thrust and a 3-second delay that works well with medium-weight rockets — ideal for weekend hobbyists, family launch days, and solo flyers who want exciting flights without stepping up to larger, more complex powerplants.

Beyond raw numbers, the C11-3 shines because of its reliability and repeatability. Whether you’re testing trim changes, teaching a new builder the basics, or simply chasing higher flights, these engines reduce the variability that can spoil a flight day. The familiar, crisp ignition and predictable delay let you tune recovery systems with confidence so recovery is clean and repairs are minimal.

Technically tuned for mid-to-high altitude performance, the C11-3 offers a total impulse of 10.00 N·s, peak thrust suitable for rockets with a max lift weight around 6.0 oz (170 g), and a short 0.80 second thrust duration that gets rockets off the pad quickly. Dimensionally these are standard 24 mm diameter motors — a match for many of our popular mid-size kits and ideal for repeat launches during a club meet or family outing.

Safety-first and user-friendly, these bulk packs include starters, starter plugs, and plenty of recovery wadding so your focus stays on flying. Always follow Estes and NAR safety guidelines when handling and installing motors, and store engines in a cool, dry place. Ready to step up your launch day? The C11-3 bulk pack is a reliable way to fill your flight schedule with consistent, thrilling launches.

title: Sidekick™
body_html:
Are two really better than one? We think so! The expertly designed Estes Sidekick manages to combine two of almost everything to produce one remarkable model rocket.

It’s a single rocket with two body tubes, two nose cones, two engine mounts, two recovery systems, and two sets of laser-cut balsa fins. Custom-cut card stock body tube joiners mate one half of this two-part flyer to the other. There’s nothing else quite like the double trouble of the Estes Sidekick.

But it doesn’t just look sharp. The cleverly designed Estes Sidekick is an excellent flier, too. This Advanced level model was created for clustered engine launches. Experience fascinating rocket flights to 700 feet under the combined thrust of two side-by-side Estes B6-4 engines.

Recoveries are dazzling to watch when the 36-inch twin mylar streamers deploy at ejection and trail the model back to earth. From ignition to touch-down, the flight of the dual-bodied Estes Sidekick rocket is not to be missed!

Eye-Catching Appearance of Estes Sidekick

Both expert and beginner model rocketeers will enjoy building the Sidekick. You’ve never worked on a rocket like this before! Precision construction is a must for this non-standard design. Finish your Estes Sidekick with the included yellow and orange, water-slide flame decals.

Put this rocket on the flight line and watch the heads turn. It’s not every day you see a clustered engine, two-in-one flying model rocket. Don’t delay! Double time it the launch field today and light up the sky with the dynamic dual delights of the Estes Sidekick!

title: LEO Space Train™
body_html:
The Challenges of Space Flight

In space flight, the first 100 miles are the toughest. It takes an enormous amount of energy to climb out of Earth's gravity and accelerate to orbital speeds. But it's at low earth orbit, or LEO, where most satellites operate, including the Leo Space Train, a proposed system for transporting people and cargo around the Earth using a train-like network of spacecraft traveling in a low Earth orbit.

Introducing the LEO Space Train

The LEO Space Train would provide a more efficient and cost-effective means of transportation compared to traditional rocket launches, making space travel more accessible and sustainable in the long run.

Enter the LEO Space Train, an innovative, reusable winged space plane now under development by the U.S. aerospace industry. Its design enables it to travel to the edge of space where it releases a piggy-back mounted, second-stage booster.

After release, the booster ignites and places the satellite payload into LEO. The LEO Space Train can be launched, recovered, and prepped for a new orbital delivery mission all in the same day.

You will enjoy bringing to life the eye-catching features that fill this impressive model rocket. The Estes LEO Space Train kit includes precision-cut balsa fin and wing panels with laser-etched details. The non-functional booster attaches to the upper surface of the main body-tube on miniature launch rails and looks like it could separate and lift away at any moment!

The Design and Functionality of the LEO Space Train

Authentic-looking plastic engine nozzles adorn the tail ends of both the powered host rocket and the non-powered booster. A sheet of different colors water slide decals with the custom LEO Space Train “lion” graphic and logo add that last touch of realism.

While the real-life counterpart to the LEO Space Train glides home to a wheels-down landing, the finished Estes kit launches and lands as a traditional model rocket.

This scale-like model can reach up to 300 feet (91 meters) on a single-stage C6-3 engine before returning gently to Earth under its own 18-inch parachute. The highly detailed LEO Space Train look great on the pad and on display. You’ll definitely want this one in your fleet!

title: Low-Boom SST™
body_html:
The Problem with Supersonic Transport

In an era of aerospace marvels, the supersonic transport (SST) stood out. By the mid-1960s, multiple nations were chasing the goal of an SST passenger jet. Imagine traveling from New York to L.A. in less than two hours – it was the verge of a revolution in air travel! But there were problems.

Budget overruns and projections of enormous operating costs were limiting the passenger SST’s appeal. But the real death knell to an international fleet of SSTs was the excessive sound – these super-fast jets were simply too noisy.

The SST’s thunderous “sonic booms” – faster-than-sound shock waves – were critically loud. The excessive noise of the SSTs led to the banning of their activity over the continental US, with other nations following suit.

Supersonic flights were eventually limited to ocean routes, causing most nations to drop their SST projects. England and France jointly developed a single model which was produced in very limited numbers. In the end, the revolution never came.

A Solution to the Sonic Boom Problem

Fast forward to today. After decades of test flights and analysis, a solution may finally be at hand: The Low-Boom SST. By adjusting critical aspects of aircraft features like nose shape, fuselage length, wing surface area, engine output, etc., researchers can cut down the duration and power of the sonic boom. Nowadays, aviation engineers are safely flying "Low-boom" supersonic test aircraft and working on passenger jet designs.

Introducing the Low-Boom SST Model Rocket:

  • Estes has created a 30-inch long, delta-winged model rocket of the next generation of quiet, super-fast passenger jets
  • The Expert level kit includes balsa-constructed, underwing engine pods and detailed water-slide decals
  • Launch the Low-Boom SST on a C6-3 engine. Watch it climb to 400 feet before gently returning under a large 15-inch parachute
  • The Low-Boom SST model rocket is a glimpse into a potential SST revolution

The SST revolution might be on its way after all!

title: Space Corps™ Lunar Scout™
body_html:
The Lunar Scout series of remote, robotic space probes was crucial to the success of the new lunar landing program of the late 2020s. This automated craft had a single, critical directive: to map the moon’s surface in exacting detail. The purpose was to identify sites for the "Second Giant Leap" lunar missions.

Designed to be inexpensive to manufacture and proven reliable after more than a dozen flawless lunar landing and mapping missions, Space Corps later adapted the rocket for exploration of Mars and its moons, Phobos and Deimos. Therefore, the adaptation allowed for exploration of Mars and its twin moons Phobos and Deimos.

The Estes Lunar Scout rocket is a lightweight model of a future historic space probe. It will play an important role in humanity’s return to the moon. With just enough detail to make this a fun but challenging build, the Lunar Scout is right for all levels of model rocket crafters.

This Intermediate-Level kit includes laser-cut cardstock fins and other parts to create an amazing flying model rocket. Intricately designed water-slide decals add an additional note of realism. The full-size Lunar Scout may not actually exist quite yet. Despite this, rocket looks real enough to do the job now!

Estes Lunar Scout Rocket: A Great Small Field Flyer

  • Compact and lightweight, the Estes Lunar Scout flies well on smaller engines.
  • You can expect the Estes A10-0T mini engine to reach a maximum altitude of 200 feet. Moreover, there are also engine options available for lower altitude flights.
  • The Lunar Scout has a featherweight recovery system, allowing it to land unharmed and be ready for another engine and flight.
  • With relatively low altitude launches and a rapid featherweight recovery, the Lunar Scout makes for a great small field flyer.

No need to wait for NASA to create their Lunar Scout – build and fly yours today!

title: Orange Bullet™
body_html:
In 1961, Vern Estes designed the first Estes model rocket packaged for sale as a complete kit: the Astron Scout™. Before launching the Astron Scout, Vern Estes created a never-before-seen prototype.

This prototype, named the Orange Bullet, used metal weights glued to the end of the fin tips to shift the center of gravity (CG) back after the engine popped out at apogee, resulting in the rocket tumbling gently instead of streamlining in nose first.

While the design functioned, Vern and fellow rocketeer G. Harry Stine decided they could achieve the same thing without ejecting the engine. In a later version that became the classic Astron Scout, they used the weight of the rocket engine itself to shift the CG backwards. Orange bullet sold tens of thousands of kits over its long lifetime and inspired countless young people to pursue technical careers.

Sixty years later, Bill Stine, G. Harry Stine's son and former Estes Vice President decided it was time for the Orange Bullet rocket to take flight. Estes' first rocket in the Designer Signature Series and the first complete kit Vern Estes ever designed, the Orange Bullet.

title: Green Eggs™
body_html:
Green Eggs lofting rocket designed for Estes C11 and D engines. However, carrying a regular size raw egg as a payload comes very close to exceeding the max lift capability of most C6 engines used in other egg loft kits. Therefore, we recommend Estes C11 engines instead. They will provide a safe and stable flight, along with a recovery suited for small-sized flying fields.

Green Eggs lofting rocket's clear payload is big enough to carry TWO medium sized eggs (with a D12-3 engine)! Swept fins allow the egg lofting rocket to stand by itself.

The main body tube and clear payload section are both the same diameter so that you can glue a standard launch lug into place without the need for an awkward stand-off. Green Eggs Balsa fins are thick enough to enhance alignment and provide exceptional strength, even when Green Eggs are mounted through a wall.

All these lofting rocket features add up to less time building and, therefore, more fun time for your students to perform experiments with their “eggstronauts”.

This kit uses the BT-65 Body Tube, Egg Capsule Nose Cone, and BT-65 Tube Coupler.

title: Destination Mars™ Leaper™
body_html:
Officially it is the LAMPMU, the Low Altitude Mars Personal Maneuvering Unit. But no one calls it that. From the first Mars Expedition of 2035 to launch fields here on Earth, it is simply known as The Leaper™. Designed as a rapid transport system between Martian surface habitats, this futuristic jetpack quickly became something more. It became fun. Pure, gravity defying fun.

The Destination Mars™ Leaper™ captures that same spirit of innovation and adventure in a model rocket unlike anything you have flown before. Why settle for ordinary when you can leap?

No Glue. No Paint. Just Pure Launch Excitement.

Built from rugged EPP foam and prefinished for a clean, mission ready look, the Leaper is engineered for quick setup and repeat flights. There is no gluing, no sanding, and no painting required. Simply insert the stabilizer rods and you are ready for the launch pad in minutes.

This beginner level rocket is ideal for new rocketeers who want something different, as well as seasoned fliers looking to add a unique spacecraft to their fleet. It is lightweight, durable, and designed to handle flight after flight.

Low Altitude Flights, Big Time Fun

Powered by recommended Estes A10 engines, including the A10-PT or A10-0T, the Leaper reaches heights up to 75 feet. That is high enough to impress your friends and family, yet low enough to easily track from liftoff to landing. Its modest altitude makes it a fantastic choice for smaller flying fields and neighborhood launch sites.

Engine installation is simple. There is no engine hook. Just wrap a few layers of masking tape around the engine for a secure friction fit, slide it into place, and you are ready for countdown.

Featherweight Recovery. Upright Landing.

At apogee, the engine ejection shifts the center of gravity, allowing the Leaper to right itself and descend gently. There is no parachute or streamer needed. Instead, it lands upright on its tripod legs, just like a true Mars survey vehicle touching down on the Red Planet.

The result is a recovery system that is simple, reliable, and incredibly cool to watch. One moment it is leaping skyward, the next it is standing tall and ready for its next mission. Mars survey complete. Prep it, load it, and leap again.

Destination Mars Awaits

With a length of 7.7 inches, a slim 0.54 inch diameter, and a launch rod size of 1/8 inch, the Destination Mars™ Leaper™ is compact, lightweight, and easy to transport. Pair it with the Porta-Pad II launch pad and your favorite Estes launch controller to complete your Mars mission experience.

If you are building out your Destination Mars collection or simply looking for a rocket that stands out on the pad, the Leaper delivers a launch experience that is fun, futuristic, and totally unforgettable. Suit up, start the countdown, and ask yourself the only question that matters. Why walk when you can leap?

Do you have a small flying field and worry about if you can recover your model rockets safely? Star Hopper is designed for small fields with it’s drag streamer recovery and Estes mini engine power. title: Star Hopper™
body_html:
The History of Star Hopper Rocket

Let's take a look at the history of Star Hopper Rocket. In June of 1947, an experienced civilian pilot reported “saucer-like discs” over Mount Rainier. Strange lights appeared in the sky before then but never like this!

By July, the papers ran stories about a rancher who discovered strange wreckage in the desert near Roswell. Accounts of mystery “aircraft” and other unknown aerial phenomena were gaining public notice. Something strange was going on and the people in charge wanted answers.

Furthermore, in 1949, a clandestine group of government scientists met at a secret airbase in Nevada to form Project Star Hopper. A fast and maneuverable piloted vehicle was the goal; meant to compete with the unidentified objects commonly referred to as "flying saucers."

With the nation’s best engineers on the task, plans were drawn up for a sleek and functional atomic-powered vessel. The goal was to launch it quickly to intercept the aggressors. The result was the Star Hopper – the world’s first interplanetary spacecraft. They constructed and tested a small fleet, and by 1955, they were ready to protect the skies from alien invaders. Or so they told us…

Competing with Flying Saucers

Was there really a Project Star Hopper? Actually, it’s hard to say. No documents or proof exists – just rumors and speculation. Consequently, based on the scant evidence available, Estes designed a detailed model of this cryptic craft. Moreover, the Estes Star Hopper is a Beginner-Level kit that all rocket lovers would like to own and fly.

This is a no-glue, no-paint, snap-together kit that anyone can build and launch all in the same day. Featuring detail-molded plastic fins, nose cone, and engine mount, this kit not only looks great but survives even the roughest landings as creators intended. Pre-finished in a retro atomic-age silver paint scheme, the Star Hopper is a stylish kit that looks great and flies even better!

Prep the Estes Star Hopper with a recommend Estes engine (not included) and get ready for fantastic flights up to 400 feet – great for demonstrations and small field flights. Besides, watch at apogee as the rocket ejects a 18-inch streamer to slow its fall and help you track it to the ground.

With the twist-on engine retainer for fast engine loading, and a relatively wide body tube for easy ejection wadding and streamer packing, you’ll have your rocket ready to launch in no time! While the real Star Hopper may only be a myth, the Estes Star Hopper is real and ready to fly!

title: Saturn 1B
body_html:
History of the Saturn 1B

Before there was the Saturn V, there was the Saturn 1B, the NASA test bed for Apollo flight hardware. The Saturn 1B test flew versions of the Apollo Command and Service Module, and the Lunar Module.

Initially tested as the second stage on the Saturn 1B rocket, the S-IVB upper stage eventually served as the third stage of the Saturn V rocket. The Saturn 1B would eventually see service as the primary launch vehicle for Earth orbit missions in the Apollo spacecraft.

Features of the Rocket

One of the distinctive features of the Saturn 1B is the set of cylindrical tanks that forms the rocket’s first stage. Sometimes people misidentify the tanks as re-purposed Redstone missile stages because they resemble a cluster of smaller rockets.

In fact, these 70-inch diameter tanks were created using the same forms that produced the Redstone rockets. So, while they share a common lineage, they were not surplus rockets themselves. The tanks fueled eight H-1 engines, four of which could gimbal to steer the rocket while under power. Eight low profile fins ringed the base of the rocket for guidance during atmospheric flight.

Saturn 1B Launches

In February of 1966, NASA launched the first Saturn 1B rocket with an early version of the Apollo Command and Service Modules. There was no crew aboard. The subsequent Saturn 1B launch of Apollo 7 on October 11, 1968 certified the Apollo spacecraft for human spaceflight. It would be the last Saturn 1B launch for nearly five years.

After the final Apollo moon landing in 1972, NASA used the last Saturn V to launch the Skylab Orbital Workshop. Three crews would eventually be sent to live and work in the space station. Each crew was launched aboard an Apollo Command Module carried by a Saturn 1B. Each launched aboard an Apollo Command Module carried by a Saturn 1B.

The first of the three Skylab crews lifted-off on Saturn 1B vehicle SA-206 and stayed for 28 days. Their first task in orbit was to repair Skylab after an accident at launch ripped away a solar panel and sun shield. Led by Apollo 12 moon walker Pete Conrad, the crew performed a dangerous EVA and successfully rescued the space station.

The Estes Saturn 1B SA-206

The Estes Saturn 1B SA-206 is a stunning 1:100 scale recreation of the Saturn 1B and Apollo spacecraft stack as it appeared in 1973 for the launch of the first Skylab crew. Every detail is there, from the Launch Escape System atop the Apollo Command and Service Module, to the first-stage H-1 engine nozzles (remove for launch).

Textured body wraps, injection molded components, and other plastic formed parts add a level of realism to this Master-Level kit that every scale modeler will appreciate. Launch your finished model using one of the recommended Estes engines for a spectacular liftoff and dazzling two-piece recovery under dual parachutes. On display or in the air, the Estes Saturn 1B is a marvelous addition to any fleet.

Reliable Sanding for Model Rockets

Building a rocket is as much about precision as it is about creativity. This 240 grit sandpaper provides excellent control for fine adjustments, whether you’re shaping delicate fins, refining nose cones, or sanding between coats of paint. Its flexibility ensures you can reach tricky areas without sacrificing quality.

Fine Grit for Smooth Finishes

240 grit is the sweet spot for smoothing surfaces before painting and for light finishing work. It removes imperfections without being overly aggressive, leaving you with a surface that’s ready for finishing touches. For builders striving for professional-quality results, this sheet is a must-have.

Durable and Easy to Use

Durable enough to handle multiple uses, this sheet is also easy to cut into smaller pieces for precise work. From body tubes to balsa wood fins, it’s a versatile accessory that delivers consistent performance and helps your rockets look their best on launch day.

Get a flawless finish on your model rocket with our 400 Grit Sandpaper. This fine-grit sheet is designed to smooth out imperfections, blend seams, and prepare surfaces for a perfect coat of paint. Fine-Tuned Precision

With its 400 grit texture, this sandpaper is ideal for achieving a smooth, even surface. Use it for final detail sanding on body tubes, nose cones, and fins to remove any minor flaws. The result is a professional-quality finish that stands out on launch day.

Wet or Dry Versatility

Durable and Reliable

Each sheet is built to last, holding up through multiple uses so you get maximum value. Whether you’re finishing a brand-new rocket or restoring an old favorite, this sandpaper ensures your build is launch-ready and visually striking.

title: Estes Tumbler
body_html:
The Estes Tumbler is more than just a drink container, it’s a statement piece for rocketeers on the go. With its 20 oz. double-wall vacuum-insulated construction, this tumbler is designed to keep hot drinks piping and cold drinks refreshing for hours, no matter where your journey takes you. Its sleek design combines everyday utility with a passion for space exploration, making it a must-have accessory for rocket lovers.

Perfect for Every Launch

Whether you’re preparing for a model rocket launch, traveling to your next adventure, or simply heading into the office, the Estes Tumbler ensures your drink stays at the perfect temperature. Its generous 20 oz. size means fewer refills and more time enjoying your favorite beverages.

Durable and Reliable

Crafted for long-lasting performance, the tumbler features a rugged build that can handle your busiest days. The double-wall vacuum insulation not only keeps your drinks at the ideal temperature but also prevents condensation, keeping your hands and surfaces dry.

Show Your Love for Rocketry

More than a functional tumbler, this piece reflects your love for rocketry and the spirit of exploration. With its clean design and rocketry-inspired branding, it’s a conversation starter and a stylish way to carry your passion everywhere you go.

title: Pro Series II™ Der Big Red Max™
body_html:
The Estes Pro Series II™ Der Big Red Max™ carries on the tradition of one of the most iconic model rockets ever made. With its oversized design and wicked style, this 29-inch tall, 3-inch diameter rocket makes a commanding presence on the launch pad and in your collection. Whether you’ve built the classic Der Red Max or are discovering it for the first time, the Big Red Max takes the fun to a whole new level.

Thrilling Lift-Offs Every Time

Known for its slow, dramatic takeoffs, the Der Big Red Max does not disappoint. When powered with an Estes F15-4 motor, expect up to 3.5 seconds of roaring smoke and fire as this beast climbs skyward. The 29mm engine mount—with no forward retainer ring—allows a wide range of engine choices, giving you the flexibility to customize every launch experience.

Strong, Durable, and Fun to Build

Building the Big Red Max is as satisfying as flying it. Featuring thru-the-wall fins for easier alignment and added strength, this rocket is designed for durability and repeat flights. With sturdy construction and clever engineering, you’ll have a reliable model that’s ready for launch after launch.

Exclusive Skull & Bones Parachute

No Red Max rocket would be complete without its signature touch. The Big Red Max includes a custom-printed 18-inch Skull & Bones parachute, making recovery a spectacle of its own. This unique feature ensures your rocket not only returns safely but also stands out with its bold personality.

For Collectors and Flyers Alike

Whether you’re a seasoned model rocketeer or someone adding to a growing collection, the Pro Series II™ Der Big Red Max™ is a must-own. It blends nostalgia, performance, and fun into a single kit that brings excitement every time you build, launch, and recover. Add it to your fleet today and experience the legend for yourself!

title: Mini AltiTrak™ Altitude Tracker
body_html:
The Estes Mini AltiTrak™ Altitude Tracker makes it easy to transform a simple rocket launch into a rich STEM learning opportunity. By using a gravity protractor to measure the angle between the student and the rocket’s apogee, the Mini AltiTrak provides the data needed to calculate altitude through basic geometry. Students can then take their results and create graphs, compare outcomes, and refine rocket designs for maximum performance.

Bring STEM to Life

Instead of just watching a rocket soar, students become active participants in the engineering and scientific process. By measuring, calculating, and analyzing, they gain a deeper understanding of aerodynamics, trajectory, and the forces that affect flight. The Mini AltiTrak fosters curiosity while teaching practical math and science skills.

Classroom-Friendly Design

Each set comes with three Mini AltiTraks, giving small groups or entire classrooms the tools they need to collaborate on flight experiments. The compact and durable design ensures these devices are easy to transport and simple to operate, making them ideal for both classroom and outdoor use.

Inspire Future Engineers

Using the Mini AltiTrak, students can experiment with different rocket designs, engine types, and launch conditions to discover how each variable impacts altitude. This hands-on approach encourages critical thinking and creative problem-solving, preparing students for deeper exploration in science and engineering.

title: Antar™
body_html:
History of Antar Model Rocket

The "Father of Model Rocketry" and founder of the National Association of Rocketry is Harry Stine (NAR #02). What's more, he is one of the original pioneers that founded the hobby right alongside Vern Estes, Stine was also a talented writer.

Estes' designers created a precise replica for this Designer Signature Series kit. Moreover, it is based on multiple sketches and the original model, which belongs to Bill Stine, Estes Vice President and the son of Harry Stine.

In 1951, people didn't have the hobby of flying model rockets yet. Therefore, they didn't design Antar as a flying model rocket. Stine was a physicist and clearly understood the science of flight. So even though Antar was a fictional vehicle, the science behind it meant it could be stable in flight.

Antar Model Rocket:

  • Initially created in 1951
  • They did not design it as a flying model rocket
  • Designed to be stable enough in flight to be used as a model rocket
  • Precise replica created for the Designer Signature Series kit by Estes' designers
  • Replica based on multiple sketches and the original model owned by Bill Stine, Estes Vice President and the son of Harry Stine

Overall, the history of the Antar model rocket is a fascinating story. It showcases the innovative and adventurous early hobbyists who laid the groundwork for modern model rocketry.

title: Rocket Stability Kit
body_html:
The Rocket Stability Kit turns model rocket design into an exciting hands-on engineering challenge. Students learn how rockets stay stable in flight by exploring important concepts like center of gravity and center of pressure, then applying those ideas as they build and test their own designs.

Explore Rocket Design Without Launch Restrictions

This kit is perfect for learning environments where access to a launch field may be limited. Instead of focusing on liftoff, students can concentrate on the engineering behind a stable rocket design and test their work using the Estes Rocket Holder.

Build, Test, Evaluate, and Redesign

With supplies for student groups to build 2 to 3 rockets, the Rocket Stability Kit gives learners the opportunity to experience the full design process. They can test their first idea, evaluate the results, make improvements, and try again, just like real engineers.

108 Rocket Configurations to Explore

Students can investigate up to 108 different rocket configurations, making every build a chance to discover how small design changes affect stability. This variety keeps the activity engaging while helping students strengthen problem-solving, observation, and critical thinking skills.

A Complete STEM Challenge Experience

The free lesson plan adds a fun mission-based challenge where students take on roles such as head of engineering, program manager, and head of manufacturing. As they work together to win a NASA contract for their design, students build communication, creativity, teamwork, and presentation skills.

title: Space Corps™ DARC-1™
body_html:
The Deep Atmosphere Research Craft is a one-of-a-kind scientific vessel developed by the Space Corps Science Division to explore the gas giants of the outer solar system. Designated DARC-1, this multi-section crewed vessel is designed for entry and maneuverability within the thick atmospheres of a Jupiter-type gaseous planet for study and exploration.

The lifting body characteristics of the DARC-1 flying model rocket are ideal for atmospheric flight in dense gases. It is capable of maintaining station under turbulent conditions, making it an excellent choice for certain types of flights. At the conclusion of its research mission, the DARC-1 initiates return by igniting and subsequently discarding its aft booster section to break atmosphere and set a trajectory for its journey home.

The DARC-1 became operational in 2052 and performed successful atmospheric surveys of Jupiter, Saturn, and some of their major moons. However, an accident over Titan caused the spacecraft to meet a tragic end.

The DARC-1 flying model rocket by Estes Industries is an expert build in the Space Corps fleet. It requires a high level of skill to assemble. Assemble each rocket in the Space Corps range to enhance your building abilities.

title: STARTECH™ Starters
body_html:
Over 60 years ago, Vern Estes helped define modern rocketry with the introduction of the first commercially available model rocket motors and starters. That legacy of safe, reliable ignition continues today with STARTECH™ Starters, engineered to honor the original design while delivering improved performance.

Enhanced Ignition Technology

At the heart of STARTECH™ Starters lies a small but powerful innovation. The nichrome wire, responsible for heating the propellant, has been coated in a specially crafted chemical compound. When activated, this compound reacts instantly with the heat of the wire, creating a concentrated burst of heat and pressure that ensures fast, consistent ignition. The result? More reliable launches and fewer misfires.

Reliable Performance Every Time

Say goodbye to launch delays and failed ignitions. Whether you’re flying your first rocket or adding to a fleet of high-altitude performers, STARTECH™ Starters deliver the dependability you need to make every launch a success. Each pack includes six starters, giving you multiple flights of proven ignition technology.

Simple, Safe, and Effective

Just like the original design, STARTECH™ Starters are easy to use and built with safety in mind. They slot seamlessly into your Estes motors, making them the perfect companion for all your launches. Safe, efficient, and highly effective, they embody the perfect blend of tradition and innovation that Estes has been known for since 1958.

title: Disposable Hobby Knife
body_html:
Take your rocket building and crafting projects to the next level with the Disposable Hobby Knife. This versatile tool is ideal for making precise cuts, trimming edges, and scraping away imperfections to achieve a flawless finish. With its pen-style body and textured grip, it feels natural in your hand and allows for detailed work with ease.

Perfect for Model Rocketry & Crafts

From shaping balsa wood fins to trimming decals, the Disposable Hobby Knife is an indispensable tool for hobbyists. It’s designed to handle the lightweight materials most commonly used in model rocketry and craft projects, ensuring clean, sharp results every time.

Precision & Comfort

The sharp, fine-point blade makes intricate cutting and scraping simple, while the ergonomic, pen-like design gives you better control and accuracy. The textured grip prevents slipping, so you can focus on getting the perfect cut without hand fatigue.

Reliable & Ready to Use

Each pack includes one disposable knife, ready to put to work in your next project. Compatible with most standard hobby blades, this tool is a reliable companion for hobbyists who demand precision and ease of use in their creative projects.

title: Blue Origin New Shepard
body_html:
The Estes Blue Origin New Shepard is a 1:66 scale model of the New Shepard launch vehicle, bringing the excitement of modern space exploration to life in a flyable rocket that is ready to launch. With its distinctive capsule and clean airframe design, this model delivers an impressive presence on the pad and a thrilling flight experience.

Designed for beginner skill levels, the Estes New Shepard arrives pre built and assembled, allowing rocketeers to focus on flying rather than construction. This makes it an excellent choice for first time flyers, families, or anyone looking for a hassle free launch experience.

Inspired by a Legacy of Space Exploration

In 1961, Alan Shepard became the first American in space, and years later he would walk on the Moon. His achievements helped define the future of human spaceflight and inspired generations to look beyond Earth.

The New Shepard name reflects that pioneering legacy, and the Estes New Shepard allows hobbyists to connect with that history through repeated launches and recoveries.

Realistic Flight and Capsule Recovery

Powered by C5-3 or C6-3 engines, the Estes New Shepard reaches projected altitudes of up to 400 feet. After ascent, the capsule deploys and descends under a large 15 inch parachute for a slow, controlled landing.

This realistic recovery sequence mirrors the mission profile of the full scale vehicle and helps protect the rocket, making it easy to prepare for another flight.

Ready to Fly Convenience and Reusability

Designed to be flown again and again, this rocket delivers dependable performance and repeatable recovery, making every launch just as exciting as the last.

title: Space Corps™ Vesta Intruder™
body_html:
In the 1950’s Enrico Fermi asked the question, if any relatively industrious and intelligent life can explore and colonize a galaxy, and intelligent life isn’t particularly rare, then intelligent alien life should be everywhere. Eventually, the Space Corps Corvette patrol encountered the large craft of unknown origin near the asteroid Vesta on June 24th, 2055. Thus, providing humanity with some answers to the question, "Where are they?"

Its purpose was unknown, its capabilities unbelievable. Besides, it had no intention of making a peaceful contact.

The Space Corps' Vesta Intruder has returned after 20 years. Today it is speeding toward the inner solar system, and the home of humanity. The Space Corps is making their last stand, and mounting a defense. Should talks not be possible, this will be a fight for the future of humanity, but traitors may receive a favorable fate from the alien conquerors. So, where will you stand?

The Space Corps Vesta Intruder is 2+ feet tall. Moreover, it can fly up to 350 feet high using a C11-3 engine! With a Standard Estes Engine, it launches loudly and disappears into the sky like a spacecraft traveling at light-speed.

The Vesta Intruder is not of human origin, and it shows from the menacing airframe to its out-of-this-world performance. Bring the Vesta Intruder to your launch site to spark ideas of intelligent communication and unknown technologies.

The main features of he Space Corps Vesta Intruder:

  • Stands over 2 feet tall.
  • Can reach altitudes of up to 350 feet on a C11-3 engine.
  • Disappears into the sky like a light-speed spacecraft upon launch.
  • Designed to inspire dreams of intelligent contact and the threat of technologies beyond human understanding.

title: Solo™
body_html:

The Solo beginner model rocket features a breakaway pod that glides to the ground, dancing through the sky during recovery, utilizing the wind and thermals to float gently to the ground. The main body of the solo comes down under parachute to touch down safely. At apogee, when the rocket reaches the peak of its flight, the pod can slide freely forward, dislodging itself from the rocket.

The main body of Solo beginner model rocket utilizes a 15 in. parachute and stands more than 2 ft. tall! Experience the flight of the Solo for yourself.

  • The Solo rocket is easy to assemble, making it perfect for beginners who are just starting out in model rocketry.
  • The breakaway pod is a unique feature that sets this rocket apart from other Beginner models on the market.
  • With a maximum altitude of 500 ft., the Solo rocket provides an exciting and thrilling flight experience.
  • The rocket is more than 2 ft. tall, making it an impressive addition to any model rocket collection.
  • The use of a 15 in. parachute for the main body of the rocket ensures a safe and gentle descent back to the ground.
  • The breakaway pod utilizes wind and thermals to float gently to the ground, providing a visually stunning recovery experience.
  • The Solo rocket is a great way to introduce young people to the world of model rocketry. Additionally, it's a great way to encourage them to explore and learn about science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) concepts.

title: B.O.S.S.™ (Belt Observer Survey Ship)
body_html:
Bill Simon collaborated with Estes to design the Belt Object Survey Ship (B.O.S.S) over 40 years ago. This was a time when the introduction of nuclear and solar power revolutionized space flight technology.

This unique rocket, which was not initially intended to be a model rocket, has been eagerly awaited and is being released as a prototype for the first time. With the B.O.S.S. Rocket, you can experience the innovation of the past with the latest addition to Estes' Signature Series.

We matched the Belt Object Survey Ship (B.O.S.S) design with premium components for top quality. Our mission is to bring you the latest in the Estes Designer Series. The B.O.S.S. Rocket comes with a rare asymmetrical structure, featuring:

Experience the beauty of space with Belt Object Survey Ship. This is a vivid testament to the ingenuity and creativity of the early space enthusiasts.

title: D12-5 Engine Bulk Pack
body_html:
The D12-5 Engine Bulk Pack is built for rocketeers who want reliable D-impulse performance in a convenient, launch-ready format. These motors are a great match for medium-weight kits and two-stage rockets that need a stronger lift-off and a predictable coast-to-recovery profile. Use them when you want added altitude and a confident, repeatable flight every time you head to the field.

Beyond raw power, the D12-5 shines because of its consistency. Each motor produces a clean, steady burn that reduces variability between flights, so you’ll see similar altitudes and flight behavior across launches. That predictability makes the D12-5 particularly useful for learning how changes in payload, fin design, or recovery systems affect performance—valuable whether you’re teaching beginners, running a club launch, or flying with the family.

Performance highlights include a total impulse of 20.00 N·s, a 5 second time delay, a maximum lift weight of about 10.0 oz (283 g), and a peak thrust of 32.90 N with a thrust duration around 1.60 seconds. These specs make the D12-5 powerful enough for rockets such as Green Eggs, Big Daddy, and Odyssey while remaining predictable and easy to manage at the launch site. The 24 mm diameter and compact form factor mean wide compatibility with many popular Estes kits and aftermarket mounts.

Ready to step up your flights? The D12-5 Engine Bulk Pack gives you the power and consistency to learn, experiment, and enjoy more successful launches. As always, follow the included safety and handling instructions, use the recommended recovery gear, and launch in a safe, legal area. title: Super Orbital Transport™
body_html:
The Estes Super Orbital Transport is an upsized redesign of a classic kit! Ultra-realistic styling and amazing parachute/glider dual recovery stand out among the rest. It includes laser-cut wooden parts and a construction jig to facilitate swift and precise assembly.

Two sheets of detailed, three-color decals complete the original look and feel of a future space liner. It launches up to 800 feet on a recommended Estes C or D engine. The Estes Super Orbital Transport looks like the real thing and flies like a dream!

The return of a classic! Initially, the original Estes Orbital Transport was a “must have” kit for a generation of rocketeers. Now, the new Estes Super Orbital Transport is here and ready to inspire a new generation!

The Estes model is inspired by the initial NASA designs for the Space Shuttle, which were intended to usher in a new era of routine and commercially-viable space travel.

The powerful booster rocket, designed to launch the passenger spacecraft into orbit, is modeled after supersonic airliners from that era. These imagined vehicles would land solely as aircraft, ready for reuse and relaunch with minimal turnaround.

New Great Features of Super Orbital Transport:

The new Estes Super Orbital transport is the bigger and updated version of the original kit. Re-engineered with laser-cut wood structural units, custom jigs to aid in accurate and speedy construction, a set of high-quality plastic nose cones, and two sheets of detailed, three-color decals to replicate the 1969 kit. This new model recreates the strikingly realistic look and feel of the original, only bigger!

Dazzling dual recoveries are the hallmark of the Estes Super Orbital Transport. Launches under the powerful thrust of the recommended Estes C or D engines are equally impressive! This model lifts off upright in the traditional rocket launch configuration. At the peak of flight, the piggy-back glider detaches and begins its winged decent while the booster section returns under its own 18 in. parachute.

The Super Orbital Transport is the Estes revival you don’t want to miss! Be part of the new tradition - build and fly this remarkable model today!

title: SpaceX Falcon 9
body_html:
SpaceX Falcon 9 Model Rocket has its own unique story. On May 30, 2020, astronauts Doug Hurley and Bob Behnken climbed aboard their Dragon Crew spacecraft. These people did something no one had ever done before : they rode a reusable commercial rocket to orbit. Thus, it marked the beginning of the Next Space Age.

Until that moment, human space flight had always been the purview of nations. Launching objects and humans into space to 'slip the surly bonds' required more resources and expertise. Neither an individual nor a corporation could afford it. Space flight was expensive. Space flight was difficult. Space flight was a rare commodity. But not anymore. Now, finally, human space flight was attainable with Falcon 9 model rocket.

Revolutionary Invention - SpaceX Falcon 9 Model Rocket

This extraordinary two-stage launch vehicle, designed and manufactured by Space X, is able to safely lift more than 50,000 lbs into orbit. Remarkably, after a successful launch, the first stage returns to Earth for an upright, powered landing and a precision touchdown, ready to launch another payload into orbit. There’s never been anything else like it!

Now, Space X has collaborated with Estes to create a 1:100 scale launchable reproduction of the Falcon 9 rocket with its Dragon Crew spacecraft payload.

And just like the actual Falcon 9 it can be re-launched over and over again!

The fully assembled scale Falcon 9 is composed of molded plastic parts with silk-screened markings and comes ready to fly.

Show off your SpaceX Falcon 9 model rocket with the included custom display stand, or store in its specially designed collectable case.

Every launch of your Estes Falcon 9 rocket will be an event! Though it won’t reach orbit, you can expect launches up to 300 feet on a recommended Estes engine. Recovery is via 18-inch parachute – sorry, powered return to pad is not a model rocket recovery option at this time!

A fantastic model on display or in flight, this Estes and SpaceX Falcon 9 collaboration belongs in your collection today!

title: 24 mm Motor Retainer Set

title: Vacuum Formed Parts (Saturn V)

Every part has been crafted to maintain historical authenticity while giving your model an impressive appearance. These details don’t just make your Saturn V look better, they bring your rocket to life. Ideal for Replacement or Restoration

title: NASA SLS
body_html:
Taller than the Statue of Liberty, NASA SLS has got more thrust than the mighty Saturn V.  The NASA SLS (Space Launch System) is ready to return humanity to the moon... and beyond!

The NASA SLS uses proven rocket technology and existing resources. It includes modified Space Shuttle main engines for its core stage and Space Shuttle-derived solid rockets for the boosters.

The NASA SLS Block1 will generate 8.8 million pounds of thrust at lift off and has enough power to carry the Orion crew, an upper stage booster, and four astronauts to lunar orbit and back.

SLS and Orion are key components of Project Artemis, the NASA program to land the first woman and the next man on the moon within the next five years.

Designed as a modular systems of components and payloads , NASA SLS model rocket can fulfil multiple roles in the course of Project Artemis.

Subsequent Block 1B and Block 2 versions of the NASA SLS will launch landers and cargo to the moon, and later to Mars.

The Estes 1:200 scale replica of this rocket portrays the Project Artemis Block 1 configuration. This is the first in the proposed series of heavy lift launch vehicles. This advanced rocket model represents America's next generation of deep space rockets. It comes pre-assembled and pre-finished with realistic markings and features, making it launch-ready.

Estes NASA SLS model rocket

Launching your NASA SLS couldn’t be easier. Prepare your rocket for flight by attaching the included transparent fins. Then load with an Estes C6-3 engine. You can expect spectacular launches up to 350 feet. Your rocket will have a graceful return to Earth under a colorful 15-inch parachute.

This rocket looks great whether counting down on the launch pad or displayed on your shelf. Between launches, show off your Estes NASA SLS with its own custom clear fins that can double as a display stand.

Perfect for Model Rockets and Beyond
